name: PixGrow Image Optimizer
author: Santosh Gautam

sections.description:
PixGrow Image Optimizer is a lightweight image compression and format conversion plugin for WordPress. Unlike traditional image optimization plugins that exhaust your server’s CPU, trigger database lockups, or force you to pay for expensive API keys, PixGrow performs the heavy lifting of image optimization client-side in your web browser using WebAssembly (Wasm).

By offloading the image compression work to your local browser (using WebAssembly-powered browser compression), you get high-quality WebP compression without third-party compression API fees, reducing hosting server CPU strain.

= ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
THE PIXGROW PHILOSOPHY:
Compress ➔ Convert ➔ Automate ➔ Restore
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ =

PixGrow is designed to be a dedicated, lightweight image-only optimizer. It does not contain bloated dashboard suites, CDNs, general page-speed tools, watermarkers, or media cleaners. It is designed to do one thing: compress and modernize your media library safely and efficiently.

The Problem: Server-Side Bloat & API Fees

Traditional image optimization plugins present major drawbacks:
1. CPU Crashes on Shared Hosting: Bulk compressing images server-side frequently causes PHP timeout errors, memory exhaustion, or account suspension on shared hosts.
2. Subscription Paywalls: Popular plugins charge monthly fees for API keys to offload compression to their servers.
3. Privacy Concerns: Sending your media library to external API endpoints exposes proprietary assets to third-party servers.

The Solution: Client-Side WebAssembly

PixGrow introduces local browser-based compression:
* Reduces Server-Side Processing: Your browser executes the compression loops locally. PixGrow is ideal for low-cost shared hosting (such as Bluehost, Hostinger, GoDaddy).
* No Third-Party Compression API Required: No API keys, no subscriptions, and no external data transmission. Your original image files remain secure within your WordPress hosting.
* Smart Next-Gen Formats: Convert JPEGs and PNGs into optimized WebP formats to improve your Google PageSpeed scores.

Features

  • Client-Side Bulk Compression: Compress your Media Library in the browser without server load.
  • Next-Gen WebP Conversion: Convert PNGs and JPEGs into high-efficiency WebP files.
  • Automatic File & DB Backups: Every optimized image is backed up, allowing you to restore original media at any time.
  • Reference Path Scanner: Find where hardcoded unoptimized image references reside in theme templates and post databases.
  • Amber Option Notice: Warning notices prevent you from navigating away or losing changes when editing settings.
  • Delete Backups Toggle: Option to preserve settings and backups on plugin uninstall or clean them up completely.

How It Works

  1. Activation: Load the plugin. When you open the dashboard, your browser compiles the secure WebAssembly compression codecs.
  2. Local Processing: The browser retrieves original images from your server, compresses them locally using your computer’s resources, and uploads the smaller WebP images.
  3. Format Update: WordPress metadata, attachment sizes, and file paths are updated.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the pixgrow-image-optimizer folder to your /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or search for “PixGrow Image Optimizer” directly in your admin dashboard.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Navigate to the PixGrow menu in the sidebar to start optimizing your images.
sections.faq:
How does PixGrow optimize images on shared hosting?

PixGrow is designed to work on shared hosting because image compression runs inside the browser instead of relying on server-side processing. This helps avoid hitting server memory limits or CPU execution caps on shared hosting providers.

How do I convert WordPress images to WebP?

PixGrow makes it easy to convert WordPress images to WebP. Simply activate the plugin, open the PixGrow dashboard, and click “Start Bulk Optimization”. Your browser will convert JPEGs and PNGs to WebP locally and replace them on your site.

Can I reduce image size without API keys?

Yes. PixGrow does not require external API keys, registration, or monthly subscriptions. It performs all calculations directly in your browser.

How does safe image replacement and restore work?

Before replacing an image with its compressed version, PixGrow creates a secure backup on your server. If you want to revert the changes, you can use the restore tool to restore your original unoptimized files safely.

Do I need to keep the PixGrow tab open during compression?

Yes. Because compression runs inside the web browser via WebAssembly, you must keep the settings tab active during bulk queues. If you close the tab, the queue will pause and resume when the page is reopened.
sections.changelog:
1.0.2

  • Fixed background automatic upload optimization pipeline.
  • Added custom event trigger window dispatch for asynchronous upload starts.
  • Updated licensing checks to support both QA constants.

1.0.1

  • Final UAT fixes and cache busting.
  • Fixed single image compression restrictions and Pro enqueues.

1.0.0

  • Initial release of PixGrow Image Optimizer.
  • Client-side WebAssembly WebP and JPEG compression.
  • Client-side WebAssembly WebP and MozJPEG format support.
  • Automatic local backups and restore functionality.
  • Visual quality comparison interface.
